Trabajar desde casa / Trabalhar de casa: Trabajar desde casa / Working from home
Há três anos, Nuria deixou o emprego num: Three years ago, Nuria left her office job in Bilbao and started working from home as a translator. At first she thought she'd have more free time, but she soon realised she found it hard to separate work from rest. So she decided that, when she finished working, she'd switch off the computer and go out for a walk. She also signed up for a pottery workshop to meet people. Today she says that, although she misses her old colleagues, she wouldn't go back to an office unless they offered her flexible hours. If she'd known, she'd have taken the step much earlier.

Como escrever e falar bem no B1: How to write and speak well at B1
PASSO 1: planeje em três partes: introdu: STEP 1: plan in three parts: introduction (topic and position), development (two or three arguments with examples) and conclusion. STEP 2: use one connector per paragraph: «en primer lugar», «por otro lado», «sin embargo», «por lo tanto», «en conclusión». STEP 3: vary your tenses: preterite and imperfect for narrating; conditional for opinion or hypothesis; subjunctive after «quiero que», «aunque», «para que», «es posible que». STEP 4: check agreement (gender, number, «el agua» is feminine), accents, the «¿ ?» and «¡ !» marks and pronoun order. STEP 5: in a formal email, open with «Estimado señor:» or «Estimada señora:», give your reason with «Le escribo para…» and close with «Quedo a la espera de su respuesta. Atentamente,». STEP 6: when speaking, give opinions and describe: «En mi opinión…», «Lo que más me interesa es…», «Estoy convencido de que…». STEP 7: if a word is missing, explain it («Es una cosa que sirve para…»); if you don't understand, ask («¿Podría repetirlo más despacio?»); if you need to think, use «A ver…» and «Déjeme pensar un momento». STEP 8: manage your time: 2 minutes to plan, 8 to write and 2 to reread.
